scope: Static integration review of local first-text timing and explicitly shared human clocks. This is not browser, native HTTP, full-duration or performance acceptance.

observations.observed: The controller remains ready until a nonempty non-delete/non-submit edit passes range/correction validation. Empty edits, setup, target appends and focus do not call start. Wrong/rejected text attempts start the same monotonic origin. Deadline checks occur before accepting subsequent edits. Test configurations and retests do not force immediate start.

Adaptive creates unstarted canonical controllers and commits actual text/composition only; refresh timer runs only in running status. Course configuration has no immediate start, and Start lesson only mounts TypingArea. Empty-Space/correction paths do not independently start timers.

Only actual human rooms call player.startAt on mount. Local bot runner/controller remain unstarted until onSnapshot sees the player timingOrigin, then both receive that exact monotonic/wall origin synchronously. Interval returns while unstarted. New generator cohort separates earlier view-started local results.

Launch arms playing with lastAt null. Only nonempty observed inserted units establish lastAt. Pause/resume before any attempts stays unstarted; active pause excludes elapsed time. Exact-deadline edits/submissions and callbacks after completion cannot add attempts.

Canonical bridge has startImmediately:false. Initial target setup is visible at elapsed0; step returns while no origin. Wrong unmatched text uses canonical reject and starts; empty, oversized refused edits and assistance metadata do not start. Canonical origin/active elapsed/actual pauses drive world, BOT, ghost and metronome; Canvas reads that active clock. Edit checks current elapsed before accepting late input. Finished phase blocks further game edits.
These intentionally retain authenticated shared server-clock startAt paths, including idle time; player first text does not restart them. Practice change does not remove those calls.
